description:
Goal: reject impossible field access at the semantic boundary where the receiver type and source span are still authoritative. Current root: LoweredStep::FieldAccess asks map_field_lookup; when a known resource(T) has no atom field named foo, semantic analysis replaces that failed lookup with any. The invalid operation then reaches backend interp as a string error and JIT/AOT as a Rust expect abort in fz_struct_get_named_field_ref.

Do not solve this primarily in the runtime. A known resource has exactly the language-defined .value projection (subject to opaque visibility); h.foo is not a dynamic struct lookup and must not be converted to any. Emit a stable source diagnostic with the field-access span when the settled receiver domain cannot support that field. Preserve conservative behavior only where the receiver genuinely may be a map/struct with an unknown field set. The runtime expect may remain an unreachable compiler-invariant guard once invalid source cannot reach it.

Acceptance: the minimal in-module resource probe fn bad(h), do: h.foo is rejected during run, interp, and build with the same telemetry-observable diagnostic and a source span; no JIT/AOT binary is executed or host-aborts; h.value remains the sole payload projection and resource_lifecycle, file_resource_lifecycle, file_handle, and resource_index_payload_private remain green; lib and clippy pass.
title: Reject impossible resource field access before backend lowering
